questions.question: What is the penalty amount specified under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024, for individuals involved in unfair practices or offenses during exams?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**up to ten lakh rupees**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024, aims to curb unfair practices in public examinations.
 
• The Bill specifies a penalty amount of **up to ten lakh rupees** for individuals involved in unfair practices during exams.
 
• This measure is intended to maintain the integrity and fairness of the examination process.
 
• The Bill includes stringent penalties to deter individuals from engaging in malpractices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unfair Means in Exams:** This includes activities such as cheating, impersonation, and use of unauthorized materials.
 
• **Legislation Purpose:** The purpose of such legislation is to enforce discipline and credibility in the education system.
 
• **Examination Integrity:** Ensuring the integrity of examinations is crucial for maintaining public trust in the education system.
 
• **Implementation:** The Bill's provisions will be implemented by examination authorities and law enforcement agencies.
 
• **Precedents:** Similar laws exist in various countries to prevent examination malpractices and uphold education standards.

questions.question: She was a Carnatic legendary singer who sang in Europe, North America and at the United Nations General Assembly. Who was she?

• She was the first Indian musician to perform at the United Nations General Assembly in **1966**.

• She received numerous awards and honors, including the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, in **1998**.

• **Philanthropy:** The act of promoting the welfare of others, typically through generous donations of money, resources, or time to charitable causes.
 
• **Legacy:** M.S. Subbulakshmi's influence on Indian classical music continues to be celebrated, and she remains an iconic figure in the world of music.

questions.question: The NBPW, which can be considered as the most widespread Iron Age pottery, stands for _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern Black Polished Ware**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) is an important category of Iron Age pottery in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is characterized by its glossy, shiny black surface.
 
• NBPW pottery is often associated with the period from around the 6th century BCE to the 2nd century BCE.
 
• It was widely used in northern India and has been found in significant archaeological sites like Pataliputra, Hastinapur, and Taxila.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Age**

 
 
• The Iron Age is the period following the Bronze Age, marked by the prevalent use of iron.
 
• In India, the Iron Age roughly started around the 12th century BCE.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Sites**
 
 
• **Pataliputra:** An ancient city in the Magadha region, which served as a capital for several Indian dynasties.
 
• **Hastinapur:** An ancient city mentioned in the Mahabharata, located in modern-day Uttar Pradesh.
 
• **Taxila:** An important archaeological site in modern-day Pakistan, associated with ancient Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Pottery**
 
 
• Pottery is one of the most significant sources of information about ancient cultures.
 
• Different styles of pottery help archaeologists date and understand ancient civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Glossy Finish**
 
 
• The glossy finish of NBPW was achieved through a complex firing process.
 
• This finish made the pottery more durable and visually appealing.

questions.question: What was the major economic challenge addressed in the Third Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**War-time expenditure and resource allocation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966) aimed to establish a self-reliant and self-generating economy in India.
 
• The major economic challenge addressed in the plan was the war-time expenditure and resource allocation due to the Indo-China War of 1962 and the Indo-Pak War of 1965.
 
• The plan had to be adjusted to accommodate increased defense spending and rehabilitation efforts.
 
• Despite these challenges, the plan also focused on agriculture, industry, and infrastructure development.
 
• The target growth rate was 5.6%, but the actual growth rate achieved was around 2.4%, partly due to the disruptions caused by the wars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-China War of 1962**

 
 
• The conflict between India and China took place between October and November 1962.
 
• It led to significant military expenditures and reallocation of resources in India.
 
• The war ended with a Chinese ceasefire on November 21, 1962.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pak War of 1965**
 
 
• The war between India and Pakistan occurred from April to September 1965.
 
• It led to substantial defense spending and resource diversion from developmental activities.
 
• The war ended following a United Nations-mandated ceasefire.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture**
 
 
• The focus on agriculture during the Third Five-Year Plan included the introduction of high-yielding variety seeds.
 
• Significant investment was made in irrigation and fertilizer production to boost agricultural output.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Growth**
 
 
• The plan emphasized the development of heavy industries and the establishment of new industrial enterprises.
 
• However, the industrial growth was lower than expected due to resource diversion to defense needs.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure Development**
 
 
• Efforts were made to expand the transportation and communication networks.
 
• Investment in infrastructure was crucial for long-term economic growth despite immediate challenges.

questions.question: Part III of the Constitution of India stated about which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Part III of the Constitution of India deals with **Fundamental Rights**, which are enshrined from Article 12 to 35.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the all-around development of individuals and are applicable to all citizens of India.
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by the courts, and individuals can approach the courts in case of any violation.
 
• They include rights such as the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• These rights act as a safeguard against any arbitrary actions of the state and ensure protection of individual liberties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality**

 
 
• It includes equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• It also includes equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and abolition of untouchability and titles.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom**
 
 
• It includes the freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and the right to practice any profession or occupation.
 
• These freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state in the interest of sovereignty, integrity, and public order.
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation**
 
 
• This right prohibits all forms of forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking.
 
• It aims to protect individuals from exploitation and abuse.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**
 
 
• It guarantees religious freedom to all citizens and ensures secularism in the country.
 
• Individuals are free to profess, practice, and propagate any religion of their choice.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• This right allows individuals to approach the Supreme Court or High Courts for enforcement and protection of their Fundamental Rights.
 
• It acts as a guardian of all other Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which sector of the economy does the Green Revolution belong to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that occurred between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• It involved the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, especially for crops like wheat and rice.
 
• The implementation of the Green Revolution included the use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and improved irrigation techniques.
 
• These advances significantly boosted food production and made countries like India self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• The Agricultural sector benefited greatly from the Green Revolution, leading to increased crop yields and food security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:** These seeds are developed to improve the productivity of crops. They are a crucial component of the Green Revolution.
 
• **Chemical Fertilizers:** Synthetic substances added to the soil to enhance its fertility and increase crop yields.
 
• **Pesticides:** Chemicals used to control pests that can damage crops, ensuring higher crop quality and quantity.
 
• **Irrigation Techniques:** Methods used to supply water to crops, which are essential for areas with inconsistent rainfall.
 
• **Food Security:** The Green Revolution played a significant role in ensuring that countries could produce enough food to meet their population's needs, reducing dependence on food imports.

questions.question: Lakshmi Vishwanathan, who won the prestigious Natya Kalanidhi Award from the Music Academy was famous for which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lakshmi Vishwanathan was an esteemed exponent of **Bharatanatyam**, a classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• She received the prestigious Natya Kalanidhi Award from the Music Academy for her extensive contributions to Bharatanatyam.
 
• Known for her exceptional **abhinaya** (expression) and intricate footwork, she brought a unique style to the traditional form.
 
• She trained under the legendary **Guru K.N. Dandayudapani Pillai**, a renowned Bharatanatyam teacher.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• It is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Originating from the temples of Tamil Nadu, it was traditionally performed by female temple dancers called **Devadasis**.
 
• The dance form is characterized by three primary elements: **Nritta** (pure dance), **Nritya** (expressive dance), and **Natyam** (dramatic dance).
 
• Bharatanatyam is accompanied by classical Carnatic music and involves a deep connection between the dancer and the divine.
 
 
 
• **Natya Kalanidhi Award**
 
 
• This prestigious award is presented by the Music Academy in Chennai to individuals who have made significant contributions to the field of dance.
 
• The award recognizes outstanding performers and teachers who have dedicated their lives to preserving and promoting classical dance forms.
 
 
 
• **Guru K.N. Dandayudapani Pillai**
 
 
• He was a legendary Bharatanatyam teacher and choreographer, known for his innovative compositions and teaching methods.
 
• His contributions to Bharatanatyam include training several prominent dancers and enriching the repertoire of the dance form.
 
 
 
• **Abhinaya**
 
 
• Abhinaya refers to the art of expression in Indian classical dance, involving facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements to convey emotions and stories.
 
• It is an essential aspect of Bharatanatyam, allowing dancers to connect with the audience and communicate complex narratives.

questions.question: When did Michael Faraday discover electromagnetic induction, the principle behind the electric transformer and generator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1831**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in the year **1831**.
 
• This discovery is crucial as it laid the foundation for the development of **electric transformers and generators**.
 
• Faraday's experiment involved moving a magnet through a coil, which generated an electric current within the coil, demonstrating the principle of electromagnetic induction.
 
• His work on electromagnetic induction is considered one of the most significant contributions to the field of electromagnetism and electrical engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**

 
 
• It is the production of voltage or electromotive force due to a change in the magnetic field.
 
• This phenomenon is the principle behind transformers, inductors, and many types of electrical generators.
 
 
 
• **Michael Faraday**
 
 
• He was an English scientist who contributed significantly to the study of electromagnetism and electrochemistry.
 
• Faraday's laws of electrolysis and his work on the Faraday effect are also notable contributions.
 
 
 
• **Electric Generators**
 
 
• Devices that convert mechanical energy into electrical energy using the principle of electromagnetic induction.
 
• Generators are widely used in power plants to produce electricity for homes and industries.
 
 
 
• **Transformers**
 
 
• Electrical devices that transfer electrical energy between two or more circuits through electromagnetic induction.
 
• They are used to increase (step-up) or decrease (step-down) voltage levels in power transmission and distribution systems.

questions.question:

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana is being implemented since ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY)** was launched in **2016** by the Government of India.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to **promote employment generation** by providing incentives to employers for generating new employment.
 
• Under PMRPY, the government pays the employer's contribution of 8.33% towards the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) for new employees for the first three years of their employment.
 
• This scheme aims to provide social security benefits and encourage employers to hire more workers in the formal sector.
 
• PMRPY is applicable to all sectors, with special focus on the manufacturing and service sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM)**

 
 
• Launched in 2019, PM-SYM is a pension scheme for unorganized workers to ensure old age protection.
 
• It provides a minimum assured pension of ₹3000 per month after the age of 60 years.
 
• The scheme is available to workers in the age group of 18-40 years with a monthly income of ₹15,000 or less.
 
• The Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) of India manages the fund and pension payouts.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, PMJJBY is a life insurance scheme providing a life cover of ₹2 lakhs for a premium of ₹436 per annum.
 
• It is available to individuals aged 18-50 years with a bank account.
 
• The cover is for one year, renewable from year to year.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, PMSBY is an accidental insurance scheme providing a cover of ₹2 lakhs for accidental death and full disability.
 
• It is available to individuals aged 18-70 years with a bank account for a premium of ₹12 per annum.
 
• The cover is for one year, renewable from year to year.
 
 
 
• **Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)**
 
 
• Launched in 2018, AB-PMJAY is the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme.
 
• It provides health cover of ₹5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
• The scheme targets more than 10 crore poor and vulnerable families (approximately 50 crore beneficiaries).

questions.question: Who were the key figures behind the recommendations that formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Chelmsford and Edwin Montagu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Chelmsford served as the Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921.
 
• Edwin Montagu was the Secretary of State for India from 1917 to 1922.
 
• The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were introduced in 1918 and formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.
 
• The reforms aimed to increase Indian participation in governance by introducing a dual system of administration known as "Dyarchy."
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919, laid the foundation for further constitutional developments in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dyarchy**

 
 
• Dyarchy was a system of double government introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919.
 
• Under Dyarchy, provincial subjects were divided into "transferred" and "reserved" categories.
 
• Transferred subjects were administered by Indian ministers, while reserved subjects remained under British officials.
 
 
 
• **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**
 
 
• The reforms sought to gradually introduce self-governance in India.
 
• It aimed to increase Indian control over domestic affairs while retaining British control over defense and foreign policy.
 
• The reforms led to the establishment of legislative councils at the provincial and central levels.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1919**
 
 
• Enacted to implement the recommendations of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
 
• Provided for a bicameral legislature at the central level.
 
• Marked a significant step towards self-governance in British India.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian National Movement**
 
 
• Although the reforms were seen as a step forward, they were criticized for not granting full self-governance.
 
• Led to increased political activity and the formation of various political groups.
 
• Set the stage for further constitutional reforms leading up to independence.

questions.question: Which are the two wettest places on Earth that receive more than 1,080 cm of rainfall in a year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cherrapunji and Mawsynram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cherrapunji** and **Mawsynram** are located in the Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• Both places experience heavy rainfall due to the orographic lift of moist air from the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **Mawsynram** holds the record for the highest average annual rainfall, which exceeds 1,080 cm.
 
• **Cherrapunji** is also known for its record-setting rainfall, often competing with Mawsynram for the title of the wettest place on Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orographic Rainfall**: This occurs when moist air is forced to rise over a mountain, cooling and condensing to form precipitation.
 
• **Meghalaya**: A state in northeastern India, known for its hilly terrain and significant rainfall.
 
• **Monsoon**: Seasonal winds that bring heavy rains, especially to the Indian subcontinent, crucial for agriculture but also causing floods.
 
• **Bay of Bengal**: A large water body in the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, contributing to the moisture-laden winds that impact rainfall in Cherrapunji and Mawsynram.

questions.question: As per National Multidimentional Poverty Index of India: A Progress Review 2023, which of the following union territories has the highest percentage of multidimensionally poor?

options.text: Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) of India: A Progress Review 2023, **Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu** has the highest percentage of multidimensionally poor among the union territories.
 
• The MPI measures poverty based on various deprivations faced by individuals across health, education, and standard of living.
 
• As per the report, the percentage of population living in multidimensional poverty in Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu is significantly higher compared to other union territories.
 
• The high poverty rate in this union territory highlights the need for targeted policy interventions to address these deprivations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

 
 
• The MPI is an international measure of acute poverty developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• It identifies multiple deprivations at the household level in health, education, and standard of living.
 
• The index helps in understanding the complexities of poverty and formulating policies to address them.
 
 
 
• **Health Indicators in MPI**
 
 
• The health dimension includes indicators such as nutrition, child mortality, and access to basic health services.
 
• These indicators highlight the need for improved healthcare infrastructure and services.
 
 
 
• **Education Indicators in MPI**
 
 
• Education indicators comprise years of schooling and school attendance.
 
• They reflect the educational attainment and access to educational opportunities for individuals.
 
 
 
• **Standard of Living Indicators in MPI**
 
 
• This dimension includes indicators such as electricity, drinking water, sanitation, housing, cooking fuel, and assets.
 
• These indicators help in assessing the living conditions and quality of life of individuals.
 
 
 
• **Policy Implications of MPI**
 
 
• The MPI provides a comprehensive framework for policymakers to address poverty in a multidimensional manner.
 
• It helps in identifying the most vulnerable groups and prioritizing areas for intervention.

questions.question: 2ⁿd October 2022 marked the __________ birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**153rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 2nd October 2022 marked the **153rd birth anniversary** of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi, born on 2nd October 1869, is widely recognized as the "Father of the Nation" in India.
 
• Gandhi Jayanti is observed across India to celebrate the life and contributions of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• This day is also celebrated globally as the **International Day of Non-Violence**, as declared by the United Nations in 2007.
 
• Various events including prayer services, commemorative ceremonies, and cultural programs are organized to honor his legacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**

 
 
• Full name: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi.
 
• He was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• Gandhi is known for his philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and civil disobedience.
 
• He led several campaigns including the Non-Cooperation Movement, the Salt March, and the Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **International Day of Non-Violence**
 
 
• Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007.
 
• It is observed on 2nd October, the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• This day is dedicated to spreading the message of non-violence through education and public awareness.
 
 
 
• **Key Events on Gandhi Jayanti**
 
 
• Prayers and tributes are offered at Raj Ghat, the memorial of Mahatma Gandhi in New Delhi.
 
• Schools and institutions organize essay competitions, art exhibitions, and plays based on Gandhi’s life and principles.
 
• Government officials and leaders pay homage to Gandhi by visiting his memorials and participating in commemorative events.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi's Influence**
 
 
• His principles of non-violence influenced global leaders like Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.
 
• Gandhi's teachings continue to inspire movements for civil rights and social justice around the world.
 
• His life and message are celebrated in literature, art, and popular culture.

questions.question: Which of the following sports was included as a discipline in the 11th Asian Games Beijing 1990?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kabaddi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kabaddi** was included as a discipline in the **11th Asian Games** held in Beijing in 1990.
 
• This was the first time Kabaddi was featured in the Asian Games, marking its debut on the international stage.
 
• India has historically been dominant in Kabaddi, winning gold medals in this sport in several editions of the Asian Games.
 
• The inclusion of Kabaddi in the Asian Games helped in promoting the sport internationally and enhancing its popularity.
 
• Kabaddi is a traditional Indian sport that involves two teams, where players take turns to raid the opponent's half to score points.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Games**: A continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia. It is the second largest multi-sport event after the Olympic Games.
 
• **Kabaddi**: A contact team sport that originated in India, played between two teams of seven players each, where the objective is to score points by raiding the opponent's half and touching as many defenders as possible.
 
• **Raid**: An act of entering the opponent's half to tag defenders and score points, while holding one's breath and chanting "Kabaddi" continuously.
 
• **Defenders**: Players from the opposing team who try to tackle and prevent the raider from returning to their half.
 
• **Scoring**: Points are scored for each opponent tagged, and the raider must return to their half without being tackled. Additional points are scored for tackling the raider successfully.

questions.question: Where were the first Asian Games held in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first Asian Games were held in **New Delhi, India** in **1951**.
 
• The event took place from **March 4 to March 11, 1951**.
 
• New Delhi was chosen as the host city due to its rapidly growing infrastructure and capability to host international events.
 
• The games were officially opened by the then President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
 
• A total of **11 nations** participated in the first Asian Games, competing in **57 events** across **8 sports**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Games Federation**

 
 
• The Asian Games are organized by the Asian Games Federation (AGF), which was later replaced by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).
 
• The AGF was established to promote sports and cultural interaction among Asian nations.
 
 
 
• **Sports in the First Asian Games**
 
 
• The sports included were Athletics, Aquatics, Basketball, Cycling, Football, Weightlifting, Wrestling, and Tennis.
 
• Japan topped the medal tally, followed by India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Asian Games**
 
 
• The Asian Games are the second largest multi-sport event after the Olympics.
 
• They serve as a platform for fostering regional cooperation and cultural exchange among Asian countries.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Asian Games**
 
 
• Since their inception, the Asian Games have grown significantly in terms of participation and the number of sports.
 
• The event is held every four years, with the next one scheduled for 2026 in Nagoya, Japan.

questions.question: Which of the following plants can be made to climb walls using special support?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pumpkin plant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pumpkin plant is a type of vine that can climb walls and other structures when provided with support.
 
• Pumpkin plants have tendrils that help them latch onto supports, enabling them to climb vertically.
 
• Supporting pumpkin plants helps maximize garden space and promotes better air circulation, reducing the risk of fungal diseases.
 
• Providing vertical support also keeps the pumpkins off the ground, reducing the likelihood of rot and pest damage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Supports:**

 
 
• Trellises: A framework of light wooden or metal bars, chiefly used as a support for fruit trees or climbing plants.
 
• Cages: Often used for growing tomatoes, these can also support pumpkin vines.
 
• Arbors: A garden structure providing vertical space for climbing plants.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Vertical Gardening:**
 
 
• Efficient use of space, particularly in small gardens.
 
• Improved air circulation, which helps prevent disease.
 
• Ease of harvesting and maintenance.
 
 
 
• **Pumpkin Varieties:**
 
 
• Small Sugar: Ideal for cooking and baking.
 
• Jack Be Little: A miniature variety perfect for decorations.
 
• Atlantic Giant: Known for producing extremely large pumpkins.
 
 
 
• **Growing Conditions:**
 
 
• Sunlight: Requires full sun for optimal growth.
 
• Soil: Prefers well-drained, fertile soil.
 
• Watering: Needs consistent moisture, particularly during fruit set.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 315 to 323**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Articles 315 to 323 of the Indian Constitution deal with the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).
 
• Article 315 provides for the establishment of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions.
 
• Article 316 outlines the appointment and term of office of members of the UPSC.
 
• Article 320 specifies the functions of the UPSC, which include conducting examinations for appointments to the services of the Union.
 
• Article 323 deals with the reports of the UPSC and the action taken on them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**

 
 
• The UPSC is India's central recruiting agency responsible for appointments to and examinations for All India services and group A & group B of Central services.
 
• It is an independent constitutional body established under Article 315 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The UPSC conducts various examinations including the Civil Services Examination, Engineering Services Examination, and Combined Defence Services Examination.
 
• The commission consists of a chairman and other members appointed by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs)**
 
 
• Similar to the UPSC, each state has its own Public Service Commission which conducts exams for state-level civil services.
 
• SPSCs are established under the provisions of Article 315 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The members of SPSCs are also appointed by the respective state's Governor.
 
 
 
• **Joint Public Service Commission**
 
 
• Article 315 also provides for the establishment of a Joint Public Service Commission for two or more states.
 
• This is established by an act of Parliament.
 
• The chairman and members of a Joint Public Service Commission are appointed by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **UPSC's Role in Recruitment**
 
 
• The UPSC is responsible for appointing officers to various civil services including IAS, IPS, IFS, and other central services.
 
• It also advises the government on matters related to recruitment, transfers, and disciplinary actions.
 
• The commission's examinations are known for their rigorous and comprehensive selection process.
